arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Goldstein argued two things are uncontested in the case.
He stated the side that brought the case is on death row, not in solitary confinement.
He described the dilemma the Court faces in disposing of the case.
Chief Justice Roberts noted the state court opinion discussed federalism issues.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case concerns federal habeas corpus review. The core dispute is whether a state court's alternate holding prevents federal courts from reviewing a Brady claim. the side that brought the case seeks federal review of the claim. the opposing side argues the state court resolved the claim on the merits.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the scope of federal habeas review. It determines when federal courts can examine state court decisions. The outcome affects the rights of death row inmates. It clarifies the relationship between state and federal courts in habeas cases.
